findings.title: The public OP Mainnet endpoint answers the elements of one batch from two op-reth builds, so a batch bracket does not pin an eth_call to a build
findings.difference: Ethereum reference endpoints used in this review answer from one build per request. mainnet.optimism.io routes each element of a JSON-RPC batch on its own, between op-reth/v2.8.1-72207294 and an unversioned op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown.
findings.mechanism: In 30 batches of three web3_clientVersion calls sent on 2026-11-26, 18 batches mixed the two builds, 11 named only the unversioned build and 1 named only v2.8.1. A batch that puts web3_clientVersion before and after an eth_call therefore does not show which build ran the call. Every opcode vector and script on OP Mainnet in this and earlier cycles ran on one of the two builds, and every one returned the specified word, so neither build was seen to compute FullMath, TickMath, BitMath or the settlement path differently. What is not shown is that each build alone ran every vector. The four rounds of the new 15,510 vector set reduce the chance that a batch never reached one build, but do not exclude it. The PoolManager computes what the block producer computes; the endpoint builds only answer reads.
findings.impact: No funds are at risk. The evidence for OP Mainnet is unpinned per build, and the unversioned build has no published source to read.
findings.preconditions: None for the routing itself. A fault would also need one of the two builds to compute an opcode differently and to be the one that produces or validates blocks.
findings.mitigations: Run pinned checks against a single-backend endpoint or a self-hosted op-reth of each version, and ask the operator which commit the unversioned build carries.

findings.title: From Lagoon a predeploy on OP Mainnet and Unichain holds type(uint128).max wei that the interop bridge releases, so native pools rest on interop message validity
findings.difference: Ethereum has no contract that can mint native ETH. OP Stack chains already credit native ETH through deposit transactions from OptimismPortal, so native pools there already rest on a bridge, and ETHLiquidity adds a second source. From Lagoon (11 January 2027, a date that depends on governance approval and can move) the ETHLiquidity predeploy on OP Mainnet and Unichain starts with type(uint128).max wei and pays ETH to SuperchainETHBridge whenever a cross-chain ETH message from the other chain is relayed, or when an expired send is refunded.
findings.mechanism: Native pools settle with msg.value and pay out with a plain value call (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364, src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). The PoolManager cannot tell where the ETH it receives came from. A relayETH on a destination chain mints from ETHLiquidity against an initiating sendETH on the source chain, and the protocol checks that link through the CrossL2Inbox access list at sequencing and through derivation. If a relay of a message that was never initiated were accepted into a canonical block, its recipient would hold ETH that no burn backs, could pay it into native pools as a normal settle and take out the other currency of every native pool up to its liquidity. Derivation replaces a block that holds an invalid executing message with a deposits-only block, which also removes the swaps made with the ETH, so in the canonical chain the ETH and the swaps vanish together. An ordinary account can send a relay transaction, but cannot make an invalid one canonical: that needs the sequencer to include it and the derivation or proof system to accept it. Before Lagoon the proxy at 0x4200..0025 has no implementation and a balance of 0 on all four Lagoon chains (queried 2026-11-26). The contract has no receive or fallback, so a native take to it reverts (ETHLiquidity.sol:63-82). F-148 records the other face of the same dependency: an unsafe reorg on one of the two chains replaces dependent blocks on the other.
findings.impact: Up to every native ETH pool on OP Mainnet and Unichain, but only through a fault in interop validation or in derivation. No path for an ordinary account was found.
findings.preconditions: Lagoon active on 11 January 2027 and a fault that lets an unbacked relayETH or refundETH become canonical, or off-chain parties acting on an unsafe block that is later replaced.
findings.mitigations: Treat interop ETH like a bridge: integrations that act on PoolManager payouts should wait for safe blocks after Lagoon. Governance can pause ETHLiquidity through the L1 pause.

cleared.check: Battery (99,985), targeted set (85,544), script sets 1 (250) and 2 (300), mined swaps and multi-step replays rerun at the builds answering on 2026-11-26.
cleared.result: No mismatch on any of the seven chains. Set 1 and set 2 give the same bytes as the Ethereum reference on all scripts. Mined swaps: OP Mainnet 2977 with 0 tick mismatches; Base 3923 with 0 tick mismatches; Unichain 6312 with 0 tick mismatches; Zora 440 with 0 tick mismatches; World Chain 186 with 0 tick mismatches; Ink 3492 with 0 tick mismatches; Soneium 494 with 0 tick mismatches.

cleared.check: New vectors for a 256 bit library that truncates the shift, byte or sign-extension index to 32 or 64 bits before clamping, or mishandles EXP exponents with only high limbs, and MULMOD, ADDMOD and the 512 bit product against moduli 2^256-1, 2^256-2, 2^256-3, 2^255+1 and (2^128-1)*2^128+1 with operands near the modulus (15,510 vectors, script cycles/027/op-stack-eth.work/scripts/hiword.py, reference from tools/opdiff/battery.py).
cleared.result: All 15,510 return the specified word on all seven chains, on OP Mainnet in four rounds. In revm-interpreter 42.0.0 and 43.0.2 SHL, SHR, SAR and BYTE clamp the index with usize::try_from over the whole word before calling ruint (macros.rs:122-126, bitwise.rs:107-158), and SIGNEXTEND compares the whole word with 31 (arithmetic.rs:126-137), so the ruint 1.19.0 fast-path truncation on Base cannot be reached. TickMath.sol:61-63 and 111, BitMath and TickBitmap therefore get specified shifts.

cleared.check: Jump destination analysis in revm-bytecode 42.0.0 (Base) and 43.0.0 (the others), and the fixes since 41.0.0.
cleared.result: The two crates have identical sources. analyze_legacy is a scalar loop that marks JUMPDEST bytes and skips PUSH1 to PUSH32 immediates (legacy/analysis.rs:10-62). The fixes of 41.0.0 and 41.0.1 (PRs 3752, 3792, 3800) replace an out-of-bounds pointer computation with wrapping_add and correct the opcode iterator used by tools; none changes which offsets are valid jump targets. The 29 JUMPDEST bytes inside the PoolManager push data therefore stay invalid targets.

cleared.check: PoolManager runtime code at each chain's address compared with the hash recorded in networks.json.
cleared.result: All seven equal the recorded length and hash, Unichain's predeploy included (24,050 bytes, 8cc5a065c50fd993).

cleared.check: Execution cache key of the reth branches behind the endpoints: op-v2.6.0-2 (op-reth v2.8.1, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, world-chain v2.8.2), op-v2.7.0-2 (op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and v2.10.0) and base-v2.5.2.11 (Base v1.5.6).
cleared.result: All three use fixed-cache 0.1.10 with storage keyed by the full (Address, StorageKey) pair, accounts by the full Address and code by the full 32 byte code hash (execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs, e.g. lines 965-971 at op-v2.7.0-2). fixed-cache compares the stored key with the requested key before returning a value (lib.rs:322-351), so a hash collision gives a miss, not another slot's value. PoolManager slots and transient deltas cannot be served from another key.

cleared.check: op-rbuilder v0.4.14 and main (revm-interpreter 41.0.0) against the nodes' 43.0.2 instruction files.
cleared.result: arithmetic.rs, bitwise.rs, control.rs, i256.rs, system.rs, memory.rs, stack.rs and macros.rs are byte identical. host.rs differs in the SSTORE cold-load skip threshold (cold_storage_additional_cost in 41.0.0, cold_storage_cost in 43.0.2). The EIP-2200 sentry rejects SSTORE with 2,300 gas or less and 100 gas is charged before the check, so the remaining gas at the check exceeds 2,200 and neither threshold is ever met. A builder on 41.0.0 computes the same results and gas for PoolManager code.

cleared.check: Base Everest phases (Base Transactions) and transient storage: can a discarded phase or the end of a phased transaction leave an unlock flag, a delta or a synced currency for later code.
cleared.result: Each phase runs under a journal checkpoint; a failed phase calls checkpoint_revert, whose journal entries revert transient storage writes (revm-context 43.0.3 journal/inner.rs:622-641), and later phases are skipped. The transaction ends in commit_tx, which clears transient storage (inner.rs:141-171), or in discard_tx on error (eip8130.rs:1815-1835). The PoolManager therefore sees the same lifetimes as in a multicall from one sender: Lock, NonzeroDeltaCount and CurrencyReserves (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36) live for one transaction, and unlock still checks the delta count before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114).

Settlement charges gas_limit times price and reports gasUsed as the limit; the opcode gas schedule and out-of-gas behaviour are unchanged. The PoolManager reads no gas price or gas used, so only the sender's fee changes.

cleared.check: L-127: every address 0x4200..0000 to 0x4200..00ff, the Base registries 0x8453..01 and 0x8453..02, the ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.7 and the WorldID contract on World Chain, called with transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(PoolManager), empty calldata and empty calldata with 1 wei, first with from set to the PoolManager and then, for the 15 that answered or matter, through a forwarder placed at the PoolManager address so that msg.sender is the PoolManager and tx.origin another account.
cleared.result: Under the real caller shape only WETH (0x06) and on OP Mainnet the OP token (0x42) accept transfer, as ordinary ERC-20s. L1BlockNumber (0x13) answers every call with the L1 block number (about 26,501,500), which Currency.transfer rejects because the word is not 1 (src/types/Currency.sol:67). Value calls succeed only at the sinks recorded in F-048 (L2ToL1MessagePasser, the four fee vaults, WETH, L1BlockNumber, the EntryPoint) and are debited to the caller first (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). L2StandardBridge rejects the PoolManager as caller; it accepted only in the plain eth_call where the PoolManager was also tx.origin. The Base registries revert every shape. 0x4200..0042 has no code on Unichain, so a take of that currency succeeds and moves nothing, which is the known no-code case of A4.

leadResults.answer: 30 three-element web3_clientVersion batches to each of the seven endpoints. mainnet.optimism.io mixed op-reth/v2.8.1-72207294 and op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown inside 18 of 30 batches; Base, Unichain, Zora, World Chain, Ink (rpc-gel) and Soneium answered one build in every batch. Recorded as a finding (operator, info). The chains 42161 and 137 of this lead belong to other units and were not queried.

op-rbuilder has no tag after v0.4.14 and main still pins revm 41.0.0 and optimism rev 85f7c13d, so no builder release names Lagoon. Its instruction files equal those of revm-interpreter 43.0.2 except the SSTORE cold-load skip threshold, which the 2,300 gas sentry makes unreachable, so a builder on it computes the same results for PoolManager code. Which builder will produce 0x7D blocks is still unknown.

Base v1.6.0-rc.4 and main link evm2 rev 9b037449 only through base-common-evm2, which no crate depends on, and its README still says it is not wired into the node. The live path is revm-interpreter 42.0.0 (v1.5.6) or 43.0.2 (rc.4), which clamps shift and byte indices on the whole word before ruint; 15,510 new large-index vectors pass on Base.
Not attempted this cycle; the unit spent its time on the interpreter angle. No new World Chain replay was run.

Unichain's refund policy is not public: refund policies are an OP Enterprise feature chosen per sequencer, released op-reth uses a null policy, and Lagoon reaches mainnet on 11 January 2027. The spec bounds each refund by the transaction's own evmGasUsed, so an ordinary account can at most recover its own gas; refunds move no PoolManager balance.

Collected 1474 of the 1,474 OP Mainnet transactions left in the cycle 24 window (optimism.drpc.org and op.api.pocket.network now serve traces for those blocks) and replayed them through the cycle 24 model from their prestate traces: 1474 transactions, 50343 words compared, 0 with a mismatch. The OP Mainnet total is now 20000 of 20,000. X Layer, Robinhood Chain, Elysium and BNB Smart Chain belong to other units.

Swept all 256 addresses of the 0x4200 range, the two Base registries and the World Chain EntryPoint and WorldID contracts with the four call shapes, then repeated the shapes through a forwarder at the PoolManager address so that the PoolManager is msg.sender and not tx.origin. Nothing beyond F-048 moves value the caller does not owe; L2StandardBridge rejects the PoolManager; L1BlockNumber's transfer answer is not 1 and is rejected by Currency.transfer.

The reth branches behind every endpoint of this unit (op-v2.6.0-2, op-v2.7.0-2, base-v2.5.2.11) use fixed-cache 0.1.10 keyed by full (Address, StorageKey), full Address and full code hash, and fixed-cache compares the full key on every hit. Celo, X Layer and Arc builds in this lead belong to other units and were not read.
